Let \(d_n=\gcd(100+n^2,2n+1)\). If \(d\mid 100+n^2\) and \(d\mid 2n+1\), then modulo \(d\):

\[
2n+1\equiv 0 \implies 2n\equiv -1 \implies 4n^2\equiv 1.
\]

Also \(100+n^2\equiv 0\), so

\[
4(100+n^2)\equiv 0 \implies 400+4n^2\equiv 0.
\]

Using \(4n^2\equiv 1\),

\[
400+1\equiv 0 \pmod d,
\]

so \(d\mid 401\). Thus \(d_n\le 401\).

This bound is attained when \(2n+1=401\), i.e. \(n=200\):

\[
a_{200}=100+200^2=40100=401\cdot 100,
\]
\[
a_{201}=100+201^2=40501=401\cdot 101.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\boxed{401}
\]
